description: One piece of hardware in the orchard that reports a number, and everything needed to decide whether to believe it. A reading is only as good as the device's calibration, its battery and how long ago it last spoke — so those live here, on the thing, rather than being repeated on every reading. `last_seen` is the field that matters most and is the one nobody sets by hand: a soil probe that has been silent for a week is not reading zero moisture, it is not reading, and the difference is a block that gets irrigated or does not.

fields.description: What it is called on the radio and on the sticker on its lid.
fields.label: Device Name

fields.description: The MAC address, serial number or IMEI printed on the unit. UNIQUE ACROSS THE SITE, and deliberately not scoped to a company: one physical box cannot be in two orchards, and a duplicate here is either a typo or a device somebody moved without re-registering.
fields.label: Hardware ID

fields.description: WHAT IT MEASURES. This is the axis that decides which reading types are plausible from this device, which is why it is the one that is required.
fields.label: Device Type
fields.options:
Soil Moisture
Flow Meter
Weather Station
Temperature
Generic

fields.description: WHAT IT DOES, which is a different question from what it measures. A gateway reports nothing of its own and relays for others; an actuator opens a valve. Kept separate from device_type because a flow meter and a valve controller sit on the same pipe and only one of them can be told to do something.
fields.label: Device Class

fields.description: The block this device sits in. Optional: a weather station on the shop roof belongs to no block, and forcing one on it would put its readings in a block's average.
fields.label: Field

fields.description: Which part of the block — 'row 14 north end', 'top of the hill'. Free text, because the sub-block a probe sits in is rarely a record anywhere.
fields.label: Zone

fields.description: Whether this device is still in service. A retired device is disabled rather than deleted, because its readings stay and a reading whose device vanished cannot be judged.
fields.label: Enabled

fields.description: The bearer token the device itself presents when posting readings. Stored as a Password field so it does not appear in a list view, an export or a print format. Generated on registration; nothing reads it back.
fields.label: Auth Token

fields.description: When this device last posted anything. READ-ONLY AND WRITTEN BY THE READING PATH, never by hand: a last_seen somebody typed is the exact field that would make a dead sensor look alive.
fields.label: Last Seen

fields.description: Percent remaining, 0 to 100. A probe below about 15% reports drifting values before it reports nothing.
fields.label: Battery Level (%)

fields.description: RSSI in dBm, so a normal value is negative — around -70 is good and -100 is nearly gone.
fields.label: Signal Strength (dBm)

fields.description: When this device was last calibrated against a known reference. An uncalibrated soil probe is a number with no units.
fields.label: Calibrated On

fields.description: Calibration coefficients, alarm thresholds, reporting interval — as JSON. Free-form on purpose: every vendor's box has a different set and none of them is worth a column.
fields.label: Device Config
